choices.term: ἀτρέπτῳ καὶ ἀμεταποιήτῳ φύσει κεῖσθαι τὸν Υἱὸν ὁμολογεῖ
choices.english: an unchangeable and unalterable nature: that is where he confesses the Son to be set
choices.why: The preposition ἐν is the last word of the previous section; the English keeps the cut and adds no bridging claim. The old English left out this whole first half of the section.

choices.english: He alone is the match of the one who begot him
choices.why: ἁμιλλάομαι, vie with, equal; the participial clause is made its own sentence.

choices.term: χθὲς καὶ σήμερον σωματικῶς ... πνευματικῶς καὶ εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας
choices.english: "yesterday and today" in the body, and the same is "forever" in the spirit
choices.why: Adverbs kept as Cyril's contrast of the bodily and the spiritual.

choices.term: τὸ λίαν εὐπάροιστον καὶ εὐδιαπτόητον τοῦ τρόπου τὴν ἀνωτάτω τοῖς ἔχουσι τιθέντος διαβολὴν
choices.english: lays the gravest charge on those whose character is easily stung into frenzy and easily scared
choices.why: εὐπάροιστος from παροιστράω (be driven mad); διαβολή here is 'charge, accusation'. The old English read 'most approachable and persuasive' and 'sets the highest value on those who possess anything', which reverses the sense.

choices.term: δίκην ὁρίζοντος τῇ νόσῳ τὴν ἀποστροφήν
choices.english: fixes his turning away as the penalty for that sickness
choices.why: The Jeremiah quotation that follows ('God took no pleasure in them') shows the turning away is God's; 'his' makes that clear without adding a claim.
The catena abbreviates the lemma; kept, not completed.

lemmas.gloss: to vie with, be the match of
(passive) to be carried away, swept aside

pass_a_gloss: [...in an] unchangeable and unalterable nature he confesses the Son to lie (be set), which is proper to the God and Father alone, and belongs to no other of the things that have come to be. Therefore, if the God and Father alone is unchangeable, and the Son also (is) in identity of nature, being always this very thing which also the one who begot him (is), how could he be one of the things that have come to be, he who alone rivals (matches) the one who begot him according to the ineffable principle of the substance, and being by nature this which the Father is, apart from only being father? For that the Word is not altered, having become a man like us, the Spirit-bearer has made known in these (words). And he makes 'yesterday' signifying the past time, and 'today' of the present, and of the future and coming (time) the 'into the ages'; and if some, receiving the 'yesterday and today' as standing for 'recent', insist (on it), how could he who is yesterday and today also be into the ages? We also will transfer the force of the question to the opposite: for the Word who is into the ages, how could he take the yesterday and today upon himself, if indeed Christ is one, and has not been divided, according to Paul's saying? Or clearly: Jesus Christ yesterday and today bodily, the same spiritually also into the ages. 'Do not be carried away by various and strange teachings.' And the 'to be carried away' has been said by metaphor from the raving (madmen), those carried around here and there; or from those easily swept aside, like reeds, easily bending toward what is always pushing, and having nothing firm; and yet, Paul having cried out 'Be steadfast, unmovable', and the Master himself putting the very-easily-stung-to-frenzy and easily-frightened (quality) of character as the highest charge against those who have it, and fixing turning-away as the penalty for the disease; for he said thus about certain people: 'They loved to move their feet and did not spare, and God was not well pleased in them'; for what is firmly and unswervingly founded is safe and inviolable toward anything whatever of the things that tend to benefit. 'For of which animals the blood is brought in', etc. And there are also very many other words about these things, but let them be passed by now because of the number; Christ, however, died according to the flesh, that he might cleanse us by his own blood. 'Therefore let us go out to him', etc. Let us bear his reproach, then, that is, the cross on our behalf; so also he himself said: 'Whoever does not take his cross and follow behind me is not worthy of me'; the [continues: 'outside the gate' ...]. [Pusey page number 418 and the printed page number 23 are not translated.]
pass_b_english: …an unchangeable and unalterable nature: that is where he confesses the Son to be set. This belongs to the God and Father alone, and to no other among the things that have come into being. So if God the Father alone is unchangeable, and the Son too is in identity of nature with him, always being just what his begetter is, how could he be one of the things that have come into being? He alone is the match of the one who begot him, by the ineffable principle of the substance, and is by nature what the Father is, except only for being Father. For the Spirit-bearer has made known in these words that the Word was not altered when he became a man like us.

He makes "yesterday" stand for time past, "today" for the present, and "forever" for what will be and is still to come (Hebrews 13:8). But if some insist on taking "yesterday and today" to mean something recent, how could the one who is "yesterday and today" also be "forever"? We too will turn the force of the question the other way: how could the Word, who is "forever," take "yesterday and today" upon himself, if Christ is one and is not divided, as Paul says (1 Corinthians 1:13)? Or, plainly: Jesus Christ is "yesterday and today" in the body, and the same is "forever" in the spirit.

"Do not be carried away by various and strange teachings" (Hebrews 13:9). "Carried away" is a metaphor taken from madmen, who are carried about this way and that; or from people who are easily swept aside, who bend readily, like reeds, toward whatever pushes them at the moment, and have nothing firm. Yet Paul cried aloud, "Be steadfast, unmovable" (1 Corinthians 15:58); and the Master himself lays the gravest charge on those whose character is easily stung into frenzy and easily scared, and fixes his turning away as the penalty for that sickness. For he said of certain people: "They loved to move their feet and did not hold back, and God took no pleasure in them" (Jeremiah 14:10). For whatever is settled firmly and without wavering is safe and secure for every purpose that leads to our good.

"For of those animals whose blood is brought in" and so on (Hebrews 13:11). There is a great deal more to say about these things, but let it be passed over now, because there is so much of it. Christ, however, died in the flesh, to cleanse us with his own blood (Hebrews 13:12). "Let us therefore go forth to him" and so on (Hebrews 13:13). Let us bear his reproach, then, that is, the cross borne for us. So he too said: "Whoever does not take up his cross and follow after me is not worthy of me" (Matthew 10:38). …

ἀτρέπτῳ καὶ ἀμεταποιήτῳ φύσει κεῖσθαι τὸν Υἱὸν ὁμολογεῖ, ὅπερ ἴδιόν ἐστι μόνου τοῦ
Θεοῦ καὶ Πατρὸς, ἑτέρῳ δὲ πρόσεστι τῶν γενητῶν οὐδενί. οὐκοῦν εἰ μόνος ἄτρεπτος ὁ
Θεὸς καὶ Πατὴρ, ἐν ταυτότητι δὲ φύσεως καὶ ὁ Υἱὸς, ἀεὶ τοῦτο ὢν ὅπερ καὶ ὁ γεννήσας
αὐτὸν, πῶς ἂν εἴη τῶν γενητῶν εἷς ὁ μόνος τῷ φύσαντι κατὰ τὸν ἄφραστον τῆς οὐσίας
λόγον ἁμιλλώμενος, καὶ τοῦτο ὢν κατὰ φύσιν, ὅπερ ἐστὶν ὁ Πατὴρ, δίχα μόνου τοῦ
εἶναι πατήρ; ὅτι γὰρ οὐκ ἀλλοιοῦται γεγονὼς ἄνθρωπος καθ' ἡμᾶς ὁ Λόγος, ἐν τούτοις
διαμεμήνυκεν ὁ πνευματοφόρος. καὶ σημαντικὸν μὲν τοῦ παρῳχηκότος χρόνου ποιεῖται
τὸ χθὲς, τοῦ γεμὴν ἐνεστῶτος τὸ σήμερον, τοῦ δὲ ἐσομένου καὶ μέλλοντος τό Εἰς τοὺς
αἰῶνας· εἰ δὲ τὸ χθὲς καὶ σήμερον ἀντὶ τοῦ προσφάτου τινὲς δεχόμενοι διατείνονται, ὁ
χθὲς καὶ σήμερον πῶς ἂν εἴη καὶ εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας; μεταστήσομεν καὶ ἡμεῖς τὴν τῆς
ἐρωτήσεως δύναμιν εἰς τὸ ἔχον ἐναντίως· ὁ γὰρ εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας ὢν Λόγος, πῶς ἂν
λάβοι τὸ χθὲς καὶ σήμερον ἐφ' ἑαυτῷ, εἴπερ ἐστὶν εἷς ὁ Χριστὸς, καὶ οὐ μεμέρισται, κατὰ
τὴν Παύλου φωνήν; ἢ δηλονότι Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς χθὲς καὶ σήμερον σωματικῶς, ὁ αὐτὸς
πνευματικῶς καὶ εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας. ∆ιδαχαῖς ποικίλαις καὶ ξέναις μὴ παραφέρεσθε.
Τὸ δὲ παραφέρεσθαι εἴρηται ἐκ μεταφορᾶς τῶν μαινομένων, τῶν τῇδε κἀκεῖσε
περιφερομένων· ἢ τῶν εὐπαρα 418 φόρως ἐν ἴσῳ δόναξιν ἐς τὸ ἀεὶ προσωθοῦν εὐκόλως
μετακλινομένων, καὶ μηδὲν βέβαιον ἐχόντων· καίτοι Παύλου μὲν διακεκραγότος
"Ἑδραῖοι γίνεσθε, ἀμετακίνητοι·" αὐτοῦ δὲ τοῦ ∆εσπότου τὸ λίαν εὐπάροιστον καὶ
